chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: 'Open the mouth of your children with water of the Euphrates and with the dust of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), so if there does not happen to be (these), so with the water of the sky (rain)'.

key_terms.تُرْبَةِ قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: Dust/earth of the grave of Al-Husayn
key_terms.حَنِّكُوا: Open the mouth (of the newborn) by placing something sweet or blessed in it

ai.seo_question: What should be used to open a newborn's mouth according to Shia hadith if Euphrates water is not available?
ai.summary: This narration highlights the Shia practice of 'tankeel' by using the sacred geography of Iraq, specifically the Euphrates and Karbala, to spiritually anchor the newborn in the lineage of Ahl al-Bayt. The hierarchy of materials—prioritizing the Euphrates and Imam Husayn’s dust over general rainwater—underscores the theological significance of place and martyrdom in Shi'i piety. This ritual serves not only as a physical blessing but as an early invocation of the Imam’s intercessory status for the child.
